data.title: Xiaomi Net Profit Likely Fell Sharply in Third Quarter — Earnings Preview
data.description:
By Jiahui Huang

Xiaomi is scheduled to report its third-quarter results on Tuesday. Here is what you need to know:

NET PROFIT: Xiaomi's net profit likely dropped 59% from a year earlier to 4.97 billion yuan, equivalent to $744.6 million, according to a poll of analysts by Visible Alpha.

REVENUE: Its revenue likely fell 5.5% to 106.92 billion yuan, according to Visible Alpha.

Xiaomi's Hong Kong-listed stock rebounded in the second half of the year, rising 17% in the three months through September and more than 8% so far this quarter, thanks to strong electric-vehicle sales momentum and easing concerns about memory-chip prices. Still, shares remains well below their mid-2025 peak. Analysts said the YU7 SUV's debut last year spurred a rerating of Xiaomi into a broader EV, AI and smart-ecosystem play from a pure consumer-electronics maker.

WHAT TO WATCH:

  • MARGIN: Xiaomi's smartphone business is expected to post stronger-than-expected gross margins due to rising average selling prices, Citi analyst s wrote in a recent note. However, margin softness likely persisted at its internet segment due to lower preinstallation income caused by weaker smartphone shipments and advertisement revenue, Citi said.
  • EV SALES: Investors will watch Xiaomi's EV margin to examine profitability at the company's newest and fastest-growing business. Citi analysts estimated that Xiaomi's EV sales price averaged 226,000 yuan in the third quarter, which would translate to a roughly 23.0 billion yuan revenue contribution from EVs for the period. Segment gross margin was likely flat sequentially at 19.3%, Citi said.
  • IOT SEGMENT: As for Xiaomi's Internet-of-Things segment, revenue from China remains pressured by a high base, while the overseas ramp-up has been slower than expected, Bernstein analysts wrote in a note. The brokerage forecast revenue for the segment to drop 14% this year, reflecting weak domestic demand.

Write to Jiahui Huang at jiahui.huang@wsj.com

data.title: Tanzania explores railway locomotive plant as East Africa seeks stronger industrial ties
data.description:
Tanzania is exploring partnerships to establish a railway locomotive manufacturing plant as part of efforts to expand domestic industrial capacity and reduce reliance on imported manufactured goods, President Samia Suluhu Hassan has announced, according to Daily News.

Hassan made the announcement in Uganda on November 19 while attending the launch of the Double Q Automotive Assembly Plant at Nakirebe in Mpigi District alongside Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni, marking the conclusion of her two-day state visit.

She did not name a partner, location or timetable for the locomotive plant, The Chanzo reported. Daily News separately reported her as saying Tanzania was exploring cooperation with Japan's Hitachi , which manufactures train engines.

Daily News said the proposed plant would build on Tanzania's railway manufacturing efforts following the commencement of metre-gauge railway locomotive assembly at the Tanzania Railways Corporation (TRC) workshop in Pugu, Dar es Salaam, in March.

Hassan urged East African Community (EAC) member states to align their industrialisation strategies and develop complementary industries rather than compete for similar investments.

“Let us turn from being consumers of imported goods to regional production and marketing hubs. We should aspire to manufacture, assemble and produce,” she said, as quoted by Daily News.

She also called for harmonised regulations governing vehicle assembly and manufacturing to support regional value chains and encourage investment across different industrial sectors.

Museveni said pooling regional resources could strengthen manufacturing, citing Tanzania's natural gas reserves and Uganda's iron ore deposits as complementary inputs for industrial production.

“Prosperity comes from business, and business means natural resources. These countries have got different natural resources. You find that Tanzania has got gas, Uganda has got iron ore and other products. So, when you put them together, instead of using them in many fragmented ways, you do better business,” he said, according to Daily News.

Hassan praised Uganda's automotive investment, saying local assembly would reduce reliance on imported second-hand vehicles and discourage the dumping of manufactured goods in the region.

Museveni also commended Double Q Motors and its Chinese partner Sinotruk (HKEX:03808) for investing in truck assembly and welcomed the company's intention to eventually use locally produced steel in vehicle components, Daily News and The Chanzo reported.

Double Q Managing Director Lin Yu said the company, which entered Uganda in 2013, became an official Sinotruk distributor in 2017 and began assembling trucks in 2020. Its new plant has an annual capacity of 4,000 trucks and plans to expand into passenger and electric vehicles. More than 5,000 trucks have already been assembled in Uganda.

Works and Transport Minister Fred Byamukama put the investment at $30mn and said the plant directly employs more than 1,200 Ugandans, Watchdog Uganda reported.

data.title: South Korean shares slump to lowest since January on AI-driven tech selloff
data.description:
Key points:
  • KOSPI falls, foreigners net sellers
  • Korean won strengthens against dollar
  • South Korea benchmark bond yield falls
  • For the midday report, please clicknL2N47400B

South Korean shares fell more than 3% on Monday as a government pledge to deploy market stabilisation funds failed to ease concerns over the AI trade and a broader technology selloff.

The benchmark KOSPI closed down 161.42 points, or 3.31%, to 4,708.54, the lowest close since January 13. The won strengthened, while the benchmark bond yield fell.

On Sunday, authorities said they would deploy market stabilisation funds immediately if conditions worsened, after the South Korean benchmark index tumbled to a 10-month low last week.

Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il on Monday reiterated plans to stabilise the stock market if needed, but the announcement fell short of specific measures and thus market expectations.

"Ongoing stock market volatility is somewhat correlated with the US stock market," a spokesperson at the presidential Blue House said during a news conference.

Chipmaker Samsung Electronics fell 3.06%, while peer SK Hynix lost 2.52%.

Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution slid 2.67%, while Hyundai Motor and sister automaker Kia Corp were down 2.94% and 2.04%, respectively.

The muted response to Seoul's policy rollout suggested investors remain more concerned about the outlook for global technology stocks than local efforts to shore up sentiment.

The sharp selloff on Monday underscores how rapidly changes in Wall Street sentiment toward AI-related spending can ripple through Asia's technology supply chain.

Investors have increasingly questioned whether massive AI investments will generate returns quickly enough to justify the costs.

The market breadth remained negative, with 824 of the 908 traded issues declining against only 71 advancers.

Foreigners were net sellers of shares worth 247.0 billion won.

data.title: ConocoPhillips to sell Norway, Teesside assets to Vår Energi for $3.9B
data.description:
ConocoPhillips  has entered into a definitive agreement to sell its Norway business and its 40.25% interest in and operatorship of the U.K. Teesside oil terminal to Vår Energi for total consideration of $4.425B, less agreed upon adjustments of approximately $0.5B as of the Jan. 1, 2026, effective date.

The transaction is expected to close by the end of the first quarter 2027 subject to approval by the Norwegian Ministry of Energy and regulatory conditions.

At closing, Vår Energi will assume the post-effective date balance sheets of the properties. Total consideration is expected to be $3.9B, including the remaining 2026 tax liability of ~$1.4B, payable in the first half of 2027, and net cash proceeds of approximately $2.5B, the company said.

Proceeds will be earmarked for general purposes and for discretionary share repurchases in 2027 to supplement the company’s long-standing commitment of returning ~45% of cash from operations to shareholders.

The transaction includes the entire issued share capital of ConocoPhillips Skandinavia AS and ConocoPhillips (U.K.) Teesside Operator Limited, which together hold the company's Norway and Teesside assets and associated decommissioning liabilities.

The Norway business includes ConocoPhillips' interests in producing assets on the Norwegian continental shelf, anchored by the operated Greater Ekofisk Area in the North Sea, as well as interests in eight partner-operated fields across the Norwegian Sea and northern North Sea. It also includes the company's interest in the Norpipe oil pipeline and certain non-operated infrastructure. The Teesside business includes the Teesside oil terminal and related pipeline infrastructure.

In 2025, the Norway business produced approximately 120 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day. Year-end 2025 proved reserves associated with the sale properties were approximately 221 million barrels of oil equivalent.

data.title: Norway's Vaar Energi to buy ConocoPhillips business for $4.43 billion
data.description:
Vaar Energi said on Monday it has agreed to buy ConocoPhillips' Norwegian upstream business and related infrastructure interests in Norway and Britain for an enterprise value of $4.43 billion.

The deal includes Norway's Greater Ekofisk Area oilfields and Britain's Teesside terminal, increasing Vaar's long-term production target to above 500,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day into the mid-2030s, the company said.

Norway's Ekofisk field, discovered by Phillips Petroleum in 1969, was the first major petroleum discovery in Norway, launching the country's oil era. Conoco acquired Phillips Petroleum in 2002.

Vaar is majority owned by Italy's Eni .

(06:47 GMT) Julius Baer Profit Climbs as Inflows Boost Assets Under Management

By Michael Hennessey

Julius Baer Gruppe reported a rise in assets under management for the first 10 months of the year, boosted by a solid stock market performance, a stronger U.S. dollar and client money inflows.

The Swiss private banking group said Monday that its assets under management stood at 553 billion Swiss francs ($658.26 billion) at the end of October, up from 546.7 billion francs at the end of June.

The increase was driven by 8.5 billion francs in net new money inflows, a positive equity-market performance and the strengthening of the U.S. dollar against the Swiss franc.

The rise in client assets boosted earnings for the year to date. The bank reported an adjusted gross margin of 82 basis points in the 10 months ended October, while adjusted pretax profit climbed 17% to 1.3 billion francs.

Julius Baer said it is still adjusting its client book to follow stricter risk rules. It aims to have the remaining planned exits--which are valued at less than 2.5% of assets under management--largely completed by the end of 2027.

The company expects IFRS and adjusted net profit for 2026 to be substantially higher than in 2025. Julius Baer also backed its financial targets for 2028.

data.title: South African rand gains as commodity prices rise and dollar weakens
data.description:
The South African rand strengthened on Monday, supported by firmer commodity prices and a weaker US dollar, which came under pressure after a Federal Reserve Governor said that the central bank's current policy rate was not high enough to curb inflation.

  • The rand traded at 17.4325 against the dollar as of 0634 GMT, about 0.9% up from its previous close

  • The dollar was softer after Fed Governor Lisa Cook made a case for more rate hikes on Friday, saying the Fed's current policy rate was not high enough to deal with inflation levels she viewed with "great concern"

  • Gold, South Africa's key export, regained some ground on Monday after falling to a 14-month low last week, while platinum gained 1.2%

  • "The big number is on Wednesday when PCE inflation data in the US is tabled... A softer or harder number will certainly push the USD this week, one way or the other, although we have seen a very sizeable move in the ZAR," said Adam Phillips, treasury specialist at Umkhulu Treasury

  • South Africa's benchmark 2035 government bond (ZAR2035=) was firmer in early deals, as the yield fell 7.5 basis points to 8.63%

data.title: Julius Baer posts net new assets below expectations as de-risking continues
data.description:
Swiss bank Julius Baer posted on Monday net new assets of 8.5 billion Swiss francs ($10.1 billion) for the year to date, falling short of a Zuercher Kantonalbank estimate of 10.5 billion francs as a de-risking process continued.

  • The annualised net new money pace of 2.0% was down from 2.8% a year earlier and below a Bank Vontobel estimate of 2.4%

  • Net new money growth was affected by the de-risking process, Julius Baer said

  • The remaining scope of exits of this alignment of the bank's client book with a revised risk and compliance framework is now clearly defined and corresponds to less than 2.5% of assets under management, the bank added

  • Julius Baer aims to have the exits largely completed by the end of 2027

  • Assets under management reached 553 billion francs by the end of October, driven by solid equity market performance, a stronger US dollar and net new money inflows, the bank said in its interim management statement for the first 10 months of 2026

  • In November the Swiss private bank launched a share buyback program of up to 600 million Swiss francs ($723 million), shortly after Swiss regulator FINMA concluded enforcement proceedings against it.

data.title: Fusionist ACE Bridge Exploit: $5.7M Loss Estimate, Bithumb Freezes Trading
data.description:
Key takeaways

  • The Fusionist ACE bridge exploit is estimated at $5.7 million across two stages, according to SlowMist, which is not an audited final total.
  • About $1.87 million in proceeds was traced to the attacker, while 53.7 million genuine ACE tokens, valued near $3.7 million, were reportedly withdrawn through the bridge.
  • Bithumb halted ACE trading on November 23 after finding signs that abnormally issued ACE had entered exchanges.
  • In the material reviewed, Fusionist has not published a reconciled loss figure or a technical post-mortem.

The Fusionist ACE bridge exploit has produced an estimated $5.7 million in losses across two stages, according to SlowMist’s incident tracker. After unbacked ACE tokens were minted on BNB Chain and sold, traders reportedly used the resulting price collapse to withdraw real ACE from the project’s Endurance bridge reserves. The fallout reached centralized exchanges on Monday, November 23: Bithumb halted ACE trading after finding indications that abnormally issued tokens had entered crypto exchanges.

This was not one attacker walking away with $5.7 million in a single transaction. The distinction matters. Roughly $1.87 million was traced through the attacker’s proceeds, while another 53.7 million genuine ACE tokens, valued around $3.7 million at the incident’s reference prices, were reportedly withdrawn through the bridge. SlowMist lists a combined $5.7 million loss estimate, not an audited final total. The bridge’s most basic promise, that a token issued on one chain corresponds to something real on another, is precisely what now needs proving.

A Privileged Minter Printed Tokens That Had No Backing

Security firm Blockaid flagged the Fusionist bridge-minter exploit on November 22. Its alert described the mechanism bluntly:

“

A privileged token-bridge minter minted unbacked ACE and sold it for USDT.

Blockaid · November 22 alert

The firm initially estimated that about $1.04 million had been extracted while the attack was still ongoing. That was an interim snapshot, not a cap on the damage.

Blockchain-monitoring account Onchain Lens subsequently reported that an attacker had routed 1,091.5 ETH, valued at about $1.87 million at the time, through Tornado Cash. That observation traces a movement of proceeds, not an extra $1.87 million to add on top of the initial extraction estimate. The values describe different points in the same suspected attacker’s fund flow.

Fusionist acknowledged an apparent ongoing ACE exploit on BNB Smart Chain on Sunday and asked users to suspend transfers, trading and bridging on that network. It has not, in the material reviewed, provided a reconciled loss figure or a technical post-mortem identifying how the privileged minting authority was abused.

A bridge minter is supposed to create a token representation only when the corresponding value is properly accounted for. Once the right to mint is misused, a chain can show perfectly ordinary-looking balances that have no matching backing.

It is a familiar failure mode: NewsBTC previously covered a bridge-role exploit that minted unbacked tokens at CrediX. That earlier case does not establish Fusionist’s root cause, but it illustrates why elevated bridge permissions are such a consequential security boundary.

Traders Found a Second Exit Through Real ACE Reserves

The subsequent drain may prove more important than the initial minting spree.

According to SlowMist’s November 22 incident entry, traders bought the sharply discounted ACE created by the market disruption and used the cross-chain bridge to withdraw about 53.7 million genuine ACE from the Endurance-side reserves. SlowMist valued that withdrawal at approximately $3.7 million.

Here is the mechanism without the jargon. A representation of ACE on BNB Chain suddenly became cheap because unauthorized supply had flooded the market. A bridge that would still accept those tokens in exchange for ACE on Endurance offered an obvious difference in value.

Anyone able to complete that conversion could receive real tokens in return for deeply discounted ones. The trading opportunity existed because the backing and the circulating representation were no longer in a trustworthy relationship.

The $3.7 million figure is a valuation of the ACE reserve outflow, not proof that every recipient sold those tokens for $3.7 million in cash. Nor does it mean every trader involved helped compromise the minter.

There is a meaningful difference between initiating the security breach and trading through a system whose defenses have already failed.

Those distinctions should not obscure the core problem. A bridge can have technically valid transactions and still produce an economically disastrous result. If unbacked supply can be redeemed for genuine reserves, the checks have failed where they matter most.

Bithumb’s Monday Halt Shows How Far the Problem Travelled

Bithumb suspended ACE deposits and withdrawals early on November 23. It then halted trading effective 7:30 a.m. Korea time, or 2:30 a.m. in Dubai, according to its follow-up ACE security notice.

The exchange said, in a translation from its Korean announcement, that it had:

“

confirmed indications that abnormally issued ACE had entered cryptocurrency exchanges.

Bithumb · ACE security notice

It identified two related BNB Chain transactions and a second transaction.

Those records are important evidence leads, but a full independent decoding of the transaction trail remains outstanding.

Bithumb’s wording is careful: it reported signs of abnormal supply entering exchanges, not a finding that every ACE token in customer accounts is invalid. The trading suspension is a protective response, not a finalized determination of customer losses.

Still, it creates a practical problem for holders who never used the bridge. If tokens are fungible within a market, exchanges and the issuer need a credible method for identifying affected supply and deciding how deposits, balances and trades will be treated.

The Real Security Question Is Why the Bridge Could Honor the Claims

There is an understandable temptation to focus on the enormous minting figures. The more consequential question is what happened when those tokens met the bridge’s reserves.

A system does not need to lose control of its entire blockchain to suffer a serious failure in one privileged contract role. Nor should a successful-looking bridge transaction count as evidence that the asset being transferred was fully backed.Our assessment

The response cannot end with a pause notice and a promise to investigate.

Fusionist needs to show which minting permissions were affected, whether they have been revoked, how much ACE was created without backing, how the Endurance-side reserve changed and what claims remain outstanding.

Exchanges need a defensible token-treatment plan, and holders need to know whether there is a shortfall and who is responsible for covering it.

There is a fair counterargument: the $5.7 million figure is an external estimate, market prices moved during the incident, and the precise compromise method is not established.

SlowMist categorizes the incident as private-key leakage, but that classification is not a substitute for an official technical finding. It would also be premature to treat a cautious exchange halt as proof that every affected customer suffered a loss.

Those qualifications change how the numbers should be reported. They do not make the underlying bridge-accounting failure less serious.

The next credible milestone is not a restored interface or a reassuring social post. It is a transparent reconciliation of the tokens minted, the reserves withdrawn and the assets still available to back legitimate ACE claims.

Until that exists, the estimated $5.7 million fallout remains a warning about both token security and the risks of trusting a bridge’s accounting.

data.title: South Korea nominates new foreign, unification ministers, spy chief
data.description:
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung reshuffled his cabinet on Monday, including three key national security posts, nominating a new spy chief and foreign and unification ministers amid calls to better manage the alliance with Washington.

Lee nominated former Justice Minister Kang Kum-sil as the new director of the National Intelligence Service (NIS), lining her up to be the country's first female spy chief.

He named a career diplomat and current deputy national security adviser, Lim Woong-soon, to be the new foreign minister and former member of parliament Hong Ik-pyo as unification minister to lead Seoul's ties with North Korea.

If appointed, the three will be tasked with shepherding Seoul's alliance with its main security ally, the United States, and improving ties with nuclear-armed North Korea, as tension simmers between the neighbours.

Seoul's fundamental policy lines on the US and the North will remain unchanged, said Lim Kwang-hyun, chief of staff at the presidential Blue House.

Cabinet and spy chief nominees are required to go through parliamentary nomination hearings but do not face votes in order to be confirmed.

Kang and Lim are expected to lead efforts to fully restore security ties with the US following Washington's partial suspension of sensitive intelligence sharing after Hong's predecessor revealed a previously unknown North Korean nuclear site.

Kang was the South's first female justice minister in 2003 and 2004 under liberal ex-President Roh Moo-hyun, spearheading his drive to reform the powerful prosecution service.

Lee, who took office in June last year, also nominated new culture and safety ministers on Monday.

data.title: Thai appeal court halves jail term of lawmaker convicted of royal insult
data.description:
Thailand's Appeals Court on Monday halved a six-year jail sentence imposed on an opposition lawmaker over a social media post deemed to have insulted the country's powerful monarchy.

Thailand has among the strictest lese majeste laws in the world, with jail terms of up to 15 years for each case of defaming, insulting or threatening the king, queen, heir apparent or regent.

People's Party lawmaker Rukchanok Srinork, a former activist known locally as "Ice", was sentenced by a lower court in 2023 to six years in prison over an X post she made in 2021 and another that she shared, in violation of lese majeste and computer crimes laws.

The court on Monday said it acquitted her of sharing the post and halved the jail term.

Pending her appeal, Rukchanok, who has denied wrongdoing, kept her seat in parliament and was re-elected in February this year.

People's Party leader Natthaphong Ruengpanyawut told reporters she was seeking bail and the process of filing an appeal to the Supreme Court was underway.

At least 199 people in Thailand were sentenced to jail terms for alleged insults of the monarchy between May 2014 and July 2026, according to the legal aid non-profit group, Thai Lawyers for Human Rights.

Under Thailand's constitution, a lawmaker can lose their seat following imprisonment under a final court judgement, subject to certain exceptions.

data.title: Malaysia's SkyeChip Sees Little Impact From New U.S. Chip Export Curbs
data.description:
By Ying Xian Wong

KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia--Malaysian chip designer SkyeChip said it expects limited fallout from new U.S. chip export restrictions.

The company, which went public in May, said Monday that its preliminary assessment found the rules were unlikely to significantly affect revenue or financial performance in the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027.

SkyeChip said it is "not involved" in data center operations. All of its 42.8 million ringgit, equivalent to around $10.4 million, in silicon product revenue in the first half of the fiscal year came from customers in North America and Northeast Asia, excluding China, it said.

The company said it is working closely with lawyers specializing in U.S. export controls and with its chip manufacturing and packaging partners to comply with the rules.

The U.S. Commerce Department issued a rule last week requiring export licences for shipments of advanced chips to Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore and Brazil. The rule aims to prevent Chinese customers from remotely using computing power at data centers in those countries. U.S. technology companies could qualify for exemptions.

Write to Ying Xian Wong at yingxian.wong@wsj.com

data.title: HCL Infosystems shares skyrocket 20% to hit upper circuit after work order from Defence Ministry – check details
data.description:
HCL Infosystems shares surged 20 percent to hit the upper circuit at Rs 11.40 on Monday, November 23, after the company announced that its subsidiary has received a Rs 138.51 crore work order from the Ministry of Defence for the upgradation of existing data center network security systems.

HCL Infosystems share price today

The stock opened at Rs 10.72 on the BSE before jumping to its upper circuit limit of Rs 11.40. HCL Infosystems had closed at Rs 9.50 in the trading session.

At around 11.55 am, the stock was trading 19.79 percent higher at Rs 11.38. The company, focused on IT support services, legacy system-integration contract closures, and receivables and litigation management, commands a market capitalisation of Rs 374.31 crore.

HCL Infosystems share price performance

The fresh order boosted buying interest in the HCL Infosystems shares, which has rallied 16.14 percent over the past one week and 14.50 percent in two weeks, according to BSE analytics.

The shares have advanced 23.32 over the past month and 2.43 percent in the past three months. The shares, however, have declined 3.15 percent in six months and 14.51 percent, on year-to-date basis.

HCL Infosystem bags order from Defence Minister

In an exchange filing shared on Friday, November 20, HCL Infosystems said that its subsidiary HCL Infotech Limited, engaged in the business of systems integration, received a change request order worth Rs 138.51 crore under an ongoing contract with the Defence Ministry.

The order involves upgrading the existing data centre network security infrastructure. The project is domestic in nature and is scheduled to be completed by July 18, 2027.

The latest work order is a part of the HCL Infotech’s ongoing contract, which is valid till the year 2031.

“HCL Infotech is required to undertake the change request order for necessary upgradation to ensure that the systems remain robust, secure and operationally efficient,” said the company in the regulatory filing.

The company clarified that the order does not involve any related-party transaction and that there is no interest from related parties in the contract.

The additional order strengthens HCL Infosystems' ongoing engagement with the Ministry of Defence and is expected to contribute to its revenue stream as the project progresses.

data.title: ABB to Buy Germany's Ziehl-Abegg for $2.22 Billion
data.description:
By Adria Calatayud

ABB said it agreed to buy Ziehl-Abegg, a German manufacturer of fans, motors and ventilation systems, for $2.22 billion.

The Swiss engineering group said Monday that the deal expands its offering for heating, ventilation and air conditioning as well as industrial-cooling applications.

Ziehl-Abegg is expected to generate about $1.4 billion in revenue in 2026 and its products are used in HVAC, data centers, clean rooms, medical technology and elevator drives, among other uses.

The acquisition aims to add electronically commutated fans to the portfolio of motors and drives of ABB's Motion business, the company said. ABB said Ziehl-Abegg's profitability is expected to be in line with that of its own operations in the area within three years after closing of the transaction, which is anticipated in the second half of 2027 subject to regulatory approvals and other customary conditions.

ABB said it intends to retain Ziehl-Abegg's headquarters in Kuenzelsau, Germany, and that it will remain committed to the country.
